The whimsical world of stream-of-consciousness writing. I love it when I get to let my thoughts wander without bounds. Here's a meandering collection of observations, ramblings, and ideas that came to mind:

Somewhere, in a small café, a flake of pastry fell from a croissant and landed on a book. The book, whose title I couldn't quite make out, was sprawled open on a small table, accompanied by a steaming cup of coffee. The flake stood defiantly on its whorled surface, like a sultan's miniature crown. The pastry was caramel-colored, a lovely accessory to the sepia tones of the aged pages.

Which reminded me of my love-hate relationship with Stationery stores. Have you ever walked into one and thought, "This is my happy place"? And yet, as I browsed the aisles lined with glitter pens, colorful paper crinkles, and wise little desk buddies, anxious thoughts creep in – did they not update this font since the Industrial Revolution?

Some people go to the ocean to find peace; I'd rather wade through racks of foliage in a grocery store. There's a smell in there that's partly plastic, partly soil, but can be perfectly comforting. Once, I saw a living Zen garden in the car park of a supermarket. Someone was meticulously tending to it, the symmetry echoing the cinematic sequences where artists meticulously prop up stones.
